answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to earn its place in a trust graph before it can move value. Each agent is a vertex, and it gains weight only through endorsements from independent, trusted peers, so a lone attacker cannot mint credibility out of thin air. Fake accounts tend to cluster together, forming a narrow ridge of mutual praise with few links to the wider meadow of real participants. When the graph shows that shape, the network can cap the cluster limits, demand extra stake, and require endorsements from outside the cluster before restoring full access.
